item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - Updated Feb 2020
item.content:encoded:
Hi canaryfarmer,

thanks for your opinion. We know the price is higher than regular games. But the fact is – we worked on the game for 7 years. It took a lot of time, money, and effort to get it done. Over 15 people worked on it – developers, graphic designers, production managers, marketing, and many others. We held over 100 betatests – each attended by at least 3 players, and they were all paid. We did original pictures on all of the 407 cards, most of them real life photos, for which we needed make-up artists, models, locations and photographers. And that’s just a few points, there is no reason to bother you with things like server and application costs, transportation, taxes, etc. - they don't provide value for you as to an SCP fan.

I’m sorry you don’t see EFS19 as more than „cards, simple game board and a tiny candle“, but there we are.

Nobody was in it for the money. We did it because we loved SCPs, and primarily wanted to make a good game. I believe we did it. Now, we want to recuperate at least some of the overall costs. I hope that isn’t much to ask, and that you understand.

item.title: Escape from Site 19 - November update
item.content:encoded:
Hello, people of the amazing SCP community and all things related!

SCP TRADEMARK

Uneasy times ahead - we cannot forget to mention the continuing issue of the Russian SCP trademark. We have witnessed the most known Russian social website, vkontakte.ru, closing down several SCP related pages, which is in no way in the spirit of the Creative Commons license of the SCP content. This keeps independent creators, like ourselves, from publishing and sharing our work in some countries, which is a shame for such a thriving SCP community. We truly hope for the resolution of this issue in favor of the Foundation so that we can keep creating, sharing and supporting each other in this amazing community.

CLIPS FROM AN UPCOMING MOVIE

But we also have some cheering news! We filmed another video this summer - and you will see the faces behind the EFS19 board game in it! We'll be publishing little clips from it very soon on our Facebook page.

CONTEST IN THE MAKING

Since we loved organizing the latest contest on our Facebook page, we already have one in mind for the future. The questions might be tougher, but the prize will also be bigger!

Hope you are excited about what there is to come! Also, happy holiday season :)

item.title: Re: SCP Board Game - Help wanted!
item.content:encoded:
Hello Gavriel

I’d like to address this concern of yours as it is sure a common issue among creators and game developers. As for our company, all of the artwork is be under CC 3.0 as usual, some of it, in fact, already used on other SCP websites. As for the SCP characters, we only add our versions of each SCP – but not for the sake of exclusivity, rather simply because there are vast possibilities of interpreting each SCP. Those are, of course, also under CC 3.0 as we, in no way, intend to pass for our own copyright with them.

We wish you a great day :)
Team EFS19

item.title: Re: SCP Board Game - Help wanted!
item.content:encoded:
I have seen some of your photo shoots on the Reddit and i do have a slight concern.

Its like this, i see you taking popular characters and changing elements of their appearance in ways that have me wondering if you are attempting to distinguish your depictions far enough away from the original art/photos so as to put your game into copyright, with a certain level of originality.

Not to own the characters themselves in any significant way, but perhaps just so your games original elements can be something other than the CC 3.0 that pretty much covers 99.999999% of everything SCP in the wiki and across the web.

I apologize if you have clarified this, one way or the other, someplace else.

So the question should be asked: Is your game going to be CC 3.0 and free for anyone to take and rework themselves after your games production/distribution?

Disclaimer: I am developing a game myself, and it will also contain original elements and it will be 100% CC 3.0 for anyone to do whatever they please with after me. Including building their own cards and expansion packs to add to my game.

Let's jump right into the exciting info!

AUGUST NEWSLETTER IN YOUR MAIL

That's right, sent out a couple of days ago! It includes the link to Behind the scenes from our summer shooting and other perks! Sign up on our website and never miss a thing!

SHOOTING AND POST-PROD

We're happy to say we finally got around to finish both the shootings and the editing of our video projects. Therefore the only thing that's left is only for us to learn how to use the video upload sites out there and upload that content (just kidding… are we?). You can now be on the lookout for not one, but two amazing videos that will help you to get to know our team and our project better!

PHOTOSHOOTING

As you probably know, all of our visual content is created by the members of our team. Therefore we decided to organize a little shooting session to provide you with new photos - namely of SCP-82, SCP-2030 and SCP-1368. Which one would you like to see first! We can make it happen :)

Anyways, we hope you had an amazing (and maybe a little bit productive) summer and we can't wait to see you in our upcoming posts!

item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - July 2019 Update

The best way to do so is, as always, by subscribing to the newsletter and follow us on social media (linked below).

STORY OF BEHIND THE SCENES

We recently posted a three-part Instagram story containing some footage from beta tests. You might be interested to take a look behind the scene that was, until now, available only via photos. If you missed the real-time story, don't worry - you can find it in our highlights!

MORE FOOTAGE TO COME

That's right. We are not stopping, in fact, we're just beginning with two very exciting video projects. You will be seeing shots and peeks of them throughout the summer and we hope you will be as excited to see the final result as we are!

TWITTER IS BACK TO LIFE!

Before reminding you of our other social media, we'd like to point out that we've been improving our twitter page which you can find here. If you want to chat or think we're missing out on a cool account that we should be following, feel free to reach us there!

This time, we offer an insight into the making of the game. There's some additional about why we need beta tests, how we do them, what feedback we got from our testers so far!

FACEBOOK ANNOUNCEMENT

Because of unfortunate things happening around the SCP trademark, we published an article explaining what it means for us as creators and also stating our views on the whole issue. You can read it here.

BETA TESTING IN ENGLISH!

A new wave of betas is about to be launched and guess what - they're in English! About the time right? This may need a little clarification: all of the previous betas have been conducted in the Czech language, cause that's where we (our team and the beta testers) are all from! Now we're going to aim at Prague expats and English speaking people, so fingers crossed!

WEBSITE REMAKE SOON

item.title: Re: Looking for work
item.content:encoded:
Hey SourBacteria,

thanks a lot and thanks for your offer. I saw your art before, I especially like your unique take on 079 and the mirror bulldog. On the cards, we actually use only real life photographs of items, areas and so on to keep up with the realism of the articles. Assistance with that would be really appreciated, though.
If you'd be able to help this way, please mail me at moc.91sfe|dnammoc5o#moc.91sfe|dnammoc5o and we can definitely figure something out.

item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - Last update 28/5/2017
item.content:encoded:
Well, or you might pull it. You never know. While SCP-231 is a challenging task, there is 299 more.

Thaumiels are not meant to be played, but are too good (as in with the flavor of the game as in "a Jumanji game", "extreme board game", "an experience" and well fitting for their SCP) to not be included.
You can play them if you want to take it to another level, of course. That we leave to the players's discretion.

item.title: Looking for work
item.content:encoded:
Hey, I'm Sourbacteria, one of the guys that makes arts for SCPs. I saw your project and I'm interested in helping out with the pictures for the cards.

You can see my arts here and here. Feel free to use any existing arts for your project, as long as I'm credited. If you want me to make new pictures for your card game, just let me know through wikidot or through the first link.

Great work, and hope I can help!

item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - Last update 28/5/2017
item.content:encoded:
Yeah. After the betatests we saw and provided a good game atmosphere, we have a catchphrase that if you play this with a group of friends, you either develop stronger bonds or start to hate each other. :D We had three couples play it, all of them left arguing. It's crazy. But it's an experience.

110 Montauk is one of the Keters that really counts on the atmosphere. And it has one of the shortest task texts, too. Beauty in simplicity.

Both 1124 and 312 are missing, but 1124 is one of the great, iconic SCPs we would like to make a task for one day.

item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - Last update 28/5/2017
item.content:encoded:
It is. Still, the Keters (about 100 cards of the hardest difficulty) make up for some crazy tasks either way. For example, 231 is not a Thaumiel, but a nasty Keter. You can see the card on our website.

We tried to incorporate 319 into the game, but so far to no avail. That doesn't mean it won't find it's way one day, however.

item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - Last update 28/5/2017
item.content:encoded: That's.. utterly horrifying and amazing at the same friggin time. Curious, but is 319 in the game? That seems like it would be a near impossible card to play.

item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - Last update 28/5/2017
item.content:encoded:
221 is already in the game, actually. As a Keter task.

The first edition of the game contains only SCPs from 0001-1999, but I am definitely thinking of future expansion packs.

item.title: Re: Escape from Site 19 - Last update 28/5/2017
item.content:encoded:
Both. Thaumiel tasks are cards that have a strict warning on them that they are not meant to be played, but we included them in the game anyway as an extra whimsical product of development, as examples of crazy tasks that would perfectly correspond to a SCP's flavor (just like how every task/card should). They are the extreme of the extreme - both physical and psychological.

There is only 9 of them and to our horror we keep finding new ones, both from Series 1 and 2. Some are famous like 012, some are little known, like 1854.
